questions.question: A mass of steam at 100Â°C is passed into water at 30Â°C. If 5 g of steam condenses to raise 50 g of water from 30Â°C to 50Â°C, calculate the specific latent heat of vaporization of water.
questions.solution:
Heat lost by steam = heat gained by water

questions.knowledgeNote: Latent heat of vaporization of water = 2260 kJ/kg. Calorimetry principle: heat lost = heat gained.
questions.answer: **Heat given out by the condensing steam** (two stages): (1) condensation at 100 °C: Q₁ = mL = 5 × L (m = 5 g); (2) the resulting water cools 100 °C → 50 °C: Q₂ = mcΔT = 5 × 4.2 × 50 = 1050 J (c = 4.2 J/g°C). **Heat gained by the cold water:** Q = mcΔT = 50 × 4.2 × (50 − 30) = 50 × 4.2 × 20 = 4200 J. **Energy balance (no losses):** Q₁ + Q₂ = Q ⟹ 5L + 1050 = 4200 ⟹ 5L = 3150 ⟹ **L = 630 J/g**. **Note:** this is far below water's accepted 2260 J/g — the given data describe a lossy or idealised experiment; the method (heat lost = heat gained) is what is examined. **Deep point:** steam problems always have *two* heat terms on the steam side — condensation at constant temperature plus cooling of the condensate; forgetting Q₂ is the classic error.
